verdict: Apple posted its best March quarter ever: revenue rose 17% to $111.2B on a record $57.0B of iPhone sales, and profit reached $29.6B.

segments.name: iPhone
segments.note: A March-quarter record on extraordinary demand for the iPhone 17 lineup; the new, cheaper iPhone 17e joined the range during the quarter.

segments.name: Mac
segments.note: Mac computers, including the new MacBook Neo launched in the quarter; up 6% YoY.

segments.name: iPad
segments.note: iPad tablets, including the M4-powered iPad Air introduced in the quarter; up 8% YoY.

segments.name: Wearables, Home and Accessories
segments.note: Apple Watch, AirPods, HomePod and accessories; up 5% YoY.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: The App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, Apple TV, Apple Pay and warranties — an all-time record, up 16% YoY, and Apple's highest-margin business.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing future products and software; up 34% YoY as Apple invests in AI and new devices.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling and admin costs, including Apple's stores; up 11% YoY.

otherDetail: Other income (expense), net was -$52M: interest and dividend income was roughly offset by interest expense and other items.
follow100Note: The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: A record March quarter for iPhone
takeaways.text: iPhone revenue hit $57.0B, up 22% — a March-quarter record, powered by the iPhone 17 lineup. iPhone alone was 51% of everything Apple sold.

takeaways.title: Services set another all-time high
takeaways.text: Services reached $31.0B, up 16%, and it is Apple's most profitable money: delivering those services cost $7.2B, against $49.2B of cost on $80.2B of product sales.

takeaways.title: A fresh buyback and a higher dividend
takeaways.text: The board authorized a new $100B share-repurchase program and raised the dividend 4% to $0.27 a share. Operating cash flow topped $28B in the quarter — both it and EPS were March-quarter records.
